title: Distances to Lines and Planes
short: Project onto a normal to find the shortest distance.

blocks.html: How far is a point from a plane? "Distance" always means the shortest distance, and the shortest path to a plane runs straight along its normal. So the question becomes a projection problem: how long is the part of a connecting vector that points along $\mathbf{n}$? The same idea, with a cross product, handles distances to lines.

Point $(x_0, y_0, z_0)$ to the plane $ax + by + cz = d$:
  $$D = \frac{|ax_0 + by_0 + cz_0 - d|}{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2 + c^2}}.$$
  Point $X$ to the line through $P_0$ with direction $\mathbf{v}$: $D = \dfrac{|\overrightarrow{P_0X} \times \mathbf{v}|}{|\mathbf{v}|}$.

Choose any point $Q$ on the plane and let $\mathbf{w} = \overrightarrow{QX}$. The distance is the length of the shadow of $\mathbf{w}$ on the normal line: $D = \frac{|\mathbf{w} \cdot \mathbf{n}|}{|\mathbf{n}|}$. Now $$\mathbf{w} \cdot \mathbf{n} = (ax_0 + by_0 + cz_0) - (a q_1 + b q_2 + c q_3) = ax_0 + by_0 + cz_0 - d,$$ because $Q$ is on the plane. Any choice of $Q$ gives the same answer, which is why the formula needs only $d$.
For a line, the parallelogram on $\overrightarrow{P_0X}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ has area $|\overrightarrow{P_0X} \times \mathbf{v}|$ and base $|\mathbf{v}|$; its height is the distance from $X$ to the line.

blocks.cap: The red dashed segment drops from $P$ to the plane along the normal. Move $P$ with the sliders: points on the same side give $ax + by + cz - d$ of the same sign, and the distance is its size divided by $|\mathbf{n}|$.

blocks.title: Point to plane
blocks.q: Find the distance from $(1, 2, 3)$ to the plane ${}2x - y + 2z = 1$.

blocks.title: Parallel planes
steps: Divide the second by 2 so the normals match: $x + 2y - 2z = 9$.
The planes $\mathbf{n} \cdot X = 3$ and $\mathbf{n} \cdot X = 9$ are $\frac{|9 - 3|}{|\mathbf{n}|}$ apart.

blocks.title: Point to line
blocks.q: Find the distance from $X(1, 1, 1)$ to the line $\mathbf{r}(t) = t\langle 1, 2, 2 \rangle$.

blocks.html: For two skew lines, the shortest connection is perpendicular to both, so it runs along $\mathbf{n} = \mathbf{v}_1 \times \mathbf{v}_2$. Project the vector between any two base points onto $\mathbf{n}$: $D = \frac{|\overrightarrow{P_1P_2} \cdot \mathbf{n}|}{|\mathbf{n}|}$.

Sign and form of the constant. The formula above is for planes written $ax + by + cz = d$, so you subtract $d$. If a plane is written $ax + by + cz + D = 0$, you add $D$ instead. Mixing the two forms changes the answer. Forgetting to divide by $|\mathbf{n}|$. The plane ${}2x + 4y + 4z = 4$ is the same plane as $x + 2y + 2z = 2$; your answer must not change when the equation is doubled, and only dividing by $|\mathbf{n}|$ makes that true.
